title: "svelte/require-store-reactive-access"
description: "Disallow to use of the store itself as an operand. Need to use $ prefix or get function"
# Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit below this line.

A store is an object with a `subscribe` method. Used as a value, in markup, a condition or a calculation, it is that object and never its current value: `{count}` prints `[object Object]`, and `if (user)` is always true. The value is `$count`, or `get(count)`.

With type information (`parserOptions.project` or `projectService` with `@typescript-eslint/parser` for the scripts of a component), anything whose type has a `subscribe` that takes two functions is a store: props, stores in `{#each}` and `{#await}`, and what a condition narrows. Without it, only the variables that `writable`, `readable` and `derived` of `svelte/store` initialize count. The fix puts a `$` before a store that is a name.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`. It uses types where the scripts of a component have `@typescript-eslint/parser` and a project:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";
import ts from "typescript-eslint";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  {
    files: ["**/*.svelte"],
    languageOptions: {
      parserOptions: { parser: ts.parser, projectService: true, extraFileExtensions: [".svelte"] },
    },
    rules: { "svelte/require-store-reactive-access": "error" },
  },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<script>
  import { writable } from "svelte/store";
  const count = writable(0);
</script>

<p>{count}</p>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<script>
  import { writable } from "svelte/store";
  const count = writable(0);
</script>

<p>{$count}</p>
```
